evidence: Two top-level packages ('budou' and 'tests') with clear separation of concerns
Core domain logic encapsulated in 'budou' package with cohesive modules (segmenter, parser, chunk, cache)
Segmenter and Parser classes use inheritance and polymorphism (ABC-based interface)
Dependency injection via factory functions (e.g., get_parser, load_cache)
No external communication endpoints (no HTTP, RPC, or messaging patterns)
All components run in same process with direct imports between modules
Test suite organized in parallel structure to source modules (tests/test_*.py)
Low directory depth (max 2) indicates flat, cohesive module hierarchy
risks: Tight coupling between Parser and concrete Segmenter implementations (violates dependency inversion)
Direct import of external libraries (html5lib, tinysegmenter) in core modules may hinder testability
Mixed responsibilities in Parser class hierarchy (parsing + authentication + preprocessing)
